revenue_by_merchant.sql:
SELECT m.merchant_name,
       SUM(t.amount) as total_revenue,
       COUNT(*) as txn_count
FROM fact_transactions t, dim_merchant m
WHERE t.merchant_id = m.merchant_id
AND t.transaction_date > '2024-01-01'
GROUP BY m.merchant_name
ORDER BY total_revenue
LIMIT 10;

issues.title: Missing filter for completed transactions
issues.problem: The query does not filter transactions by status to only include completed transactions.

issues.title: Implicit join syntax
issues.problem: Using implicit join syntax can make the query less readable.
issues.fix: FROM fact_transactions t JOIN dim_merchant m ON t.merchant_id = m.merchant_id

issues.title: Lack of comments
issues.problem: The query lacks comments explaining the logic and purpose.
issues.fix: /* Calculate total revenue and transaction count for merchants with completed transactions after 2024-01-01 */

review.corrected_sql: SELECT m.merchant_name, SUM(t.amount) as total_revenue, COUNT(*) as txn_count FROM fact_transactions t JOIN dim_merchant m ON t.merchant_id = m.merchant_id WHERE t.status = 'COMPLETED' AND t.transaction_date > '2024-01-01' GROUP BY m.merchant_name ORDER BY total_revenue LIMIT 10;
review.summary: The query has a correctness issue by not filtering for completed transactions and uses implicit join syntax. Adding comments would improve readability.

customer_spend.sql:
SELECT c.customer_name, c.email, c.tier,
       SUM(t.amount) as lifetime_value,
       COUNT(t.transaction_id) as total_orders
FROM dim_customer c
LEFT JOIN fact_transactions t ON c.customer_id = t.customer_id
WHERE t.status = 'COMPLETED'
GROUP BY c.customer_name, c.email
HAVING SUM(t.amount) > 1000
ORDER BY lifetime_value DESC;

issues.title: Incorrect lifetime_value calculation
issues.problem: The query is summing all transaction amounts without filtering by status, which should only include 'COMPLETED' transactions.
issues.fix: SUM(CASE WHEN t.status = 'COMPLETED' THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END) as lifetime_value

issues.title: Missing filter for 'COMPLETED' status
issues.problem: The WHERE clause should be in the JOIN condition to ensure all customers are included, even those without completed transactions.
issues.fix: LEFT JOIN fact_transactions t ON c.customer_id = t.customer_id AND t.status = 'COMPLETED'

issues.title: Lack of comments on complex logic
issues.problem: The HAVING clause lacks a comment explaining why only customers with a lifetime value over $1000 are being filtered.
issues.fix: -- Only include customers with a lifetime value over $1000

issues.title: Inconsistent naming convention
issues.problem: The alias 'lifetime_value' could be more descriptive, such as 'total_completed_value'.
issues.fix: SUM(CASE WHEN t.status = 'COMPLETED' THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END) as total_completed_value

review.corrected_sql: SELECT c.customer_name, c.email, c.tier, SUM(CASE WHEN t.status = 'COMPLETED' THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END) as total_completed_value, COUNT(t.transaction_id) as total_orders FROM dim_customer c LEFT JOIN fact_transactions t ON c.customer_id = t.customer_id AND t.status = 'COMPLETED' GROUP BY c.customer_name, c.email HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN t.status = 'COMPLETED' THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END) > 1000 ORDER BY total_completed_value DESC;
review.summary: The query had correctness issues with the lifetime value calculation and missing filter in the JOIN condition. Readability was improved by adding comments and renaming aliases.

daily_failure_rate.sql:
SELECT transaction_date,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fact_transactions f2
        WHERE f2.status = 'FAILED'
        AND f2.transaction_date = t.transaction_date) as failed_count,
       COUNT(*) as total_count,
       failed_count / total_count * 100 as failure_rate
FROM fact_transactions t
GROUP BY transaction_date
ORDER BY transaction_date;

issues.title: Incorrect calculation of failure rate
issues.problem: The failure rate is being calculated incorrectly because failed_count is not defined in the SELECT clause but used in the calculation.

issues.title: Correlated subquery
issues.line: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fact_transactions f2 WHERE f2.status = 'FAILED' AND f2.transaction_date = t.transaction_date
issues.problem: The correlated subquery can be inefficient as it runs for each row in the outer query.
issues.fix: Use a JOIN to pre-aggregate the failed counts.

issues.title: Lack of comments on complex logic
issues.problem: The query lacks comments explaining the logic, especially around the calculation of failure rate.
issues.fix: Add comments to explain the logic.

review.corrected_sql:
WITH failed_transactions AS (SELECT transaction_date, COUNT(*) AS failed_count FROM fact_transactions WHERE status = 'FAILED' GROUP BY transaction_date)
SELECT t.transaction_date,
       f.failed_count,
       COUNT(*) AS total_count,
       COALESCE(f.failed_count, 0) / COUNT(*) * 100 AS failure_rate
FROM fact_transactions t
LEFT JOIN failed_transactions f ON t.transaction_date = f.transaction_date
GROUP BY t.transaction_date, f.failed_count
ORDER BY t.transaction_date;
review.summary: The query had correctness issues with the failure rate calculation, performance issues with a correlated subquery, and readability issues with lack of comments. The corrected query addresses these issues.
